Method.Name: registerSignIn
friendlyName

AxTableField.Name: DeviceId
AxTableField.Label: Device ID
AxTableField.HelpText: Generated on the handheld itself and stable for the life of the install - not a hardware serial number.

AxTableField.Name: FriendlyName
AxTableField.Label: Friendly name
AxTableField.HelpText: Brand and model together, e.g. "Zebra TC27". Recomputed on every sign-in.

AxTableField.Name: Platform
AxTableField.Label: Platform
AxTableField.HelpText: "Android" today - this app has no other client - but reported by the device rather than assumed, the same as the standard Warehouse app's own device list, so a future non-Android client needs no schema change here.

AxTableField.Name: PlatformVersion
AxTableField.Label: Platform version
AxTableField.HelpText: The OS version, e.g. "14". Useful the same way AppVersionName is - a fault that only shows up on some handhelds often turns out to be an OS-version line, not a device-model one.

AxTableField.Name: AppVersionName
AxTableField.Label: App version
AxTableField.HelpText: The app build last signed in from this device. Useful when a fault only shows up on some handhelds - the first question is usually whether they are all on the same build.

AxTableField.Name: LastWarehouseId
AxTableField.Label: Last warehouse
AxTableField.HelpText: The signed-in worker's default warehouse as of their last sign-in - not necessarily where the device is right now if they later switched warehouses without signing out.

AxTableField.Name: IsActive
AxTableField.Label: Active
AxTableField.HelpText: Deactivate a device that has been retired or lost. It can still sign in - deactivating a device is fleet bookkeeping, not a remote lock - but drops off the active-fleet view.
